MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 15, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m. on August
15, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 11, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Ury

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  August 15, 2011
 CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council continued their evaluation of the City
Manager and advanced to a conclusion but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Piano Performance by Carl Hankey Middle School Student Shelby Wong

  Pianist Shelby Wong played for the City Council Members and the audience.

P2.  Certificate of Appreciation to Robert Minich

  Mayor Leckness presented a Certificate of Appreciation to Robert Minich.

P3.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners

  Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the senior family recycling award to
  Jan "Micky" and Marie Scholte.

P4.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of commendation to Lance Corporal Daniel
  Godina and Sergeant Cory L. Kingston.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: on behalf of a Casta del Sol resident, she reported that there is a sign on
Jeronimo directing pedestrians to cross the street; however there is no cross walk. She suggested
that a cross walk with warning lights and signs could be placed near Casta del Sol gate 2.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  August 15, 2011

23.  Safe Routes to School (CIP 208): Pedestrian/Bicycle Safety and Circulation Plans-

City Council Minutes  5  August 15, 2011
 27.  Provide Permission to Athens Street Sweeping to Use the City Contracted Rate for

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject program to Tom Bistline Construction Inc. for the

  license agreement with Tom Bistline Inc., for the period of September 1, 2011, through

PUBLIC HEARINGS

29.  Appeal filed by Council Member Cathy Schlicht and Council Member Rhonda
  Reardon of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s July 11, 2011 approval
  of Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99,
  being petitions submitted by Tom Bergerson, agent for UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP,
  to demolish an existing 120,000 sq. ft. (approx.) former K-Mart building and
  construct a three-level apartment complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos
  Boulevard, in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone. The project will
  consist of 320 apartments and 671 parking spaces, of which 525 will be in a three-
  level parking structure with roof deck parking. Of the development’s 320 units, 48
  units are proposed as affordable at very low and low income. Minor Exception
  ME2011-99 is submitted to allow a height increase for some minor architectural
  details and chimney vents above the City’s 35-foot height limit. This project will
  replace a previously approved project by UDR for 250 for-sale town home units at
  this site which has expired.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Planning Manager Elaine Lister provided a history of the former K-Mart property and
  outlined the proposed project for apartments at the site.

  The City Council Members disclosed any meetings they have had with the developer
  and/or members of the public and whether or not they have visited the project site.

City Council Minutes  6  August 15, 2011
   Jeremy Cyr and Tom Bergerson, UDR: outlined the project and displayed a PowerPoint
  presentation depicting the proposed Los Alisos apartment complex.

  Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing at 7:41p.m.

  The following made comments in opposition to the proposed apartment complex citing
  size, density and potential traffic issues: Donald Landis, M.V.; Sam Cohen, M.V.; Frank
  Gilliland, M.V.; Cliff Swan, M.V.; John Sobczak, M.V.; Mike Lepre, M.V.; Carl
  Hungerford, M.V.; Susan Hungerford, M.V.; Anthony De John, M.V.; Doris De John,
  M.V.; Teruko Kawai, M.V.; Dale Sandore, M.V.; Sandra Sukhov, M.V.; Alice
  Zimmerman, M.V.; Eugene "Pat" Coyle, M.V.; Marian Coyle, M.V.; Betty Gilliland,
  M.V.; Gail Reavis, M.V.; Sara (Sally) Maynard, M.V.; Natalie Parsons, M.V.; and Eva
  Schmidler, M.V.

  The following expressed support for the proposed apartment complex: Emily Osterberg,
  Apartment Association of Orange County; Linda Tang, The Kennedy Commission; and
  Dan Avery, M.V.

  The following presented a written comment recommending that the project be limited to
  250 townhomes: Connie Lee, M.V.

  Jeremy Cyr, UDR: responded to comments made during the public hearing and
  responded to questions of the City Council.

  Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing at 9:44 p.m.

RECESS

At the hour of 9:10 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
9:21 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to confirm
  the Planning and Transportation Commission’s Action by Denying the Appeal and
  Adopting Resolution 11-54 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and
  Minor Exception ME2011-99, and by Adopting a Mitigated Negative Declaration for
  Proposed Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  7  August 15, 2011
 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to continue the
meeting past the posted adjournment time.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None

30.  Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2011 - Phase 2

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented staff report.

  Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing at 11:01 p.m. Upon hearing no comments
  from members of the public, he closed the public hearing at 11:01 p.m.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to instruct
  the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in
  accordance with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

31.  Ordinance Electing to Comply With and Participate in the Alternative Voluntary
  Redevelopment Program Contained in Part 1.9 of Division 24 of the California
  Health and Safety Code; Resolution of Enforceable Obligations Payment Schedule;
  and Resolution Making an Election in Connection with Serving as Successor Agency

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and noted that the California Supreme
  Court’s recent action will prevent the City Council from adopting the Ordinance that is
  presented. He further outlined his recommendation that the City Council adopt the
  proposed resolutions as a safety net and to maintain the City’s list of enforceable
  obligations.

City Council Minutes  8  August 15, 2011
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  CDA Resolution of 11-11 Adopting an Enforceable Obligation Payment Schedule
  Pursuant to part 1.8 of Division 24 of the California Health and Safety Code and Taking
  Certain Actions in Connection Therewith; and (2) adopt Resolution 11-55 Making an
  Election in Connection with Serving as a Successor Agency Under Part 1.85 of Division
  24 of the California Health and Safety Code and Taking Certain Actions in Connection
  Therewith.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 11-50 Changing the Established Meeting Date for the Planning Commission;

City Council Minutes  9  August 15, 2011
   and (2) direct staff to post Summary Minutes on the web site within 48 hours of the

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury deferred the report to the next meeting.

  Mayor Leckness deferred the report to the next meeting.

City Council Minutes  10  August 15, 2011
 37.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

38.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley informed the community that she is hosting a blood drive on Friday,
September 9, 2011, in the Saddleback Room at city hall. The blood drive is in honor of those
who lost their lives on September 11, 2001, and she invited residents to contact her for an
appointment or register on line at www.redcrossblood.org, using sponsor code COMV. She
further announced that she is working with a Boy Scout troop to plan a special observance of
9/11 to be held at Civic Center on September 11, 2011, at 8:00 a.m. Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of August is self control.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she attended the Senior Community Activity Team
(SCAT) volunteer luncheon and a ceremony and luncheon at the Orange County Fair where she
helped serve food to the "VIP" foster families and foster children. She also had the opportunity
to listen to State Controller John Chang and she found his presentation to be very straight
forward and extremely interesting. Council Member Reardon noted that she volunteered at the
Prelude in the Park event alongside Administrative Services Director Cheryl Dyas and it was a
great event. Lastly, she asked her colleagues and the community to continue praying for young
Cade Spinello who is recovering from cancer.

Council Member Schlicht

City Council Minutes  11  August 15, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht announced that she would delay her comments regarding recent
activities and instead she would dedicate her remarks this evening to the Navy Seals that were
killed on August 2 in a helicopter crash. She noted that this was the group that brought closure
to 9/11 when they killed Osama Bin Laden and in their honor she quoted Thomas Jefferson:
"The tree of liberty must be refreshed from time to time with the blood of patriots and tyrants"
and General George S. Patton: "It is foolish and wrong to mourn the men who died, rather we
should thank God that such men lived."

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury asked the City Clerk to post, on line, a copy of his PowerPoint presentation
and the public records request that he presented for item 29.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he attended the grand opening of the LA Fitness on Alicia
Parkway and he encouraged residents to go and visit the facility.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:36 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 6, 2011 at 5:00 p.m.
